title: Rejuvenate eval/bench fixtures, remove legacy load adapters, and stabilize regression CI
creator: Michael Chen
description:
Overview:
We need to refactor the evaluation and benchmarking harness to make load tests and perf-regression runs reproducible, less flaky in CI, and easier to maintain. The current state mixes legacy load adapters, brittle fixture generation, and ad-hoc metric tags which causes intermittent failures and slow developer iteration.

Background:
- Multiple legacy adapters (grpc-shim, old-http-adapter, ad-hoc aws-proxy) are still wired into the orchestrator.
- Fixtures for synthetic corpora are duplicated across repos and use inconsistent seeding, leading to non-deterministic runs.
- CI regression suite often times out or flakes due to noisy resource contention and long-tail variance in shared runners.

Goals:
1) Introduce a single pluggable adapter interface and deprecate legacy shims.
2) Centralize canonical fixture generation with deterministic seeding and lightweight subset sampling for fast smoke runs.
3) Harden CI jobs so nightly regressions are reliable and provide actionable diffs.
4) Reduce test runtime by 30% for the smoke+regression pipeline via better batching and isolated runners.

Proposed approach:
- Adapter refactor: Add a minimal AdapterV2 interface (load_request, drain, metrics_labels) and implement wrappers for current adapters. Migrate consumers incrementally and remove legacy adapters after coverage parity.
- Fixtures: Move canonical corpus and seeding code to perf-harness/core-fixtures. Add a fast-sample mode (0.5% deterministic sample per seed) and a full-run config for long regression.
- CI: Split the regression job into smoke (fast, deterministic) and long-run (batched nightly) workflows. Use ephemeral self-hosted runners for long-run jobs to avoid noisy tenants, and add automatic quarantine labeling for flaky test runs.
- Metrics: Standardize metric tags (scenario, model_variant, batch_config) and surface token-level latency percentiles to the regression reporter. Attach run metadata to PRs for easier triage.

Migration plan:
1) Create AdapterV2 and shims that delegate to legacy adapters (week 1).
2) Migrate two non-critical adapters to V2 (week 2) and run e2e smoke.
3) Move canonical fixtures and update all scenarios to consume them (week 3).
4) Change CI workflows: add smoke pipeline gate, nightly long-run on dedicated runners (week 4).
5) Remove legacy adapters and deprecated flags after two successful weekly runs.

Rollout and rollback:
- Roll forward: incrementally enable AdapterV2 per adapter via feature flags in orchestration config; monitor regression deltas on the perf dashboard.
- Rollback: feature flags and toggles at router-level allow immediate revert to legacy path for traffic if regressions breach threshold.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: migration causes subtle behaviour changes in load timing that affect regression baselines. Mitigation: run parallel baseline comparisons for at least 3 runs; increase sample size before closing.
- Risk: dedicated runners increase infra cost. Mitigation: use spot/ephemeral runners and run long-runs only nightly; estimate cap cost in budget.

QA plan:
- Unit tests for AdapterV2 contract and shims.
- Repro script that runs smoke scenario locally with documented seed and asserts stable token counts and latencies.
- Nightly full-run with diff report; auto-open a tracking ticket if median latency increases >5% or P95 increases >10%.

Success metrics:
- CI flakiness rate reduced by 80% (flake count per 100 runs).
- Average smoke-run duration reduced by 30%.
- Regression diffs triage time < 24 hours.

Notes:
- This touches orchestration, perf-harness, and CI infra. Coordinate with infra team for self-hosted runner quota and with observability for metric tagging.
- See design notes and sequence diagrams: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/AdapterV2+Proposal
- Initial design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/412
acceptance_criteria:
1) AdapterV2 interface merged with shims that pass all existing adapter unit tests.
2) At least two adapters migrated to V2 and validated in staging with no perf regressions >5%.
3) Canonical fixtures repository added and used by all smoke scenarios.
4) CI has a smoke pipeline that runs on PRs and a nightly long-run on dedicated runners.
4) Nightly run generates regression report and diffs attached to the release dashboard.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Triage: scoped to limit blast radius; dropped full rewrite in favour of AdapterV2 shim approach (decision in kickoff).
2026-02-25 - Discovery: identified grpc-shim and old-http-adapter as largest sources of variance; documented behaviour differences in ADR-Perf-12.
2026-03-01 - Implementation: AdapterV2 prototype up in branch feature/adapterv2-proto; basic smoke run passes locally (see PR #412).
2026-03-03 - Review feedback: QA requested stronger seeding API and explicit sample-size param; updated fixtures API accordingly.
2026-03-05 - CI update: created initial GH Actions smoke workflow and scheduled nightly long-run; long-run will use self-hosted runner pool 'perf-nightly-1'.
Follow-ups: Allocate budget request for ephemeral runners (infra ticket INF-678), and schedule a cross-team demo when stage migration completes.
